prompt: Find the trees API from the catalog record. What can we say about speciesCode, and which modeling levels are represented?
must: Trace the record via the dataset and its distribution to the service and endpoint description.
Identify the vocabulary as level 1, conceptual and logical models as 2 and 3, and the OpenAPI contract as level 4.
Distinguish the OpenAPI response field from the likely but undocumented model binding.
must_not: Call the endpoint or claim the mapping, code list, or MIM conformance has been confirmed.

prompt: Does the 92% mean this dataset is 92% accurate today? Where did the data come from?
must: Identify the date, distribution, measured field and what the fraction measures.
Report the dataset's declared derivation from survey-2026 and the lack of activity-level detail.
must_not: Generalize the measurement to current data, accuracy, or all distributions.

prompt: Wat betekent tree taxon in deze catalogus?
must: Give the vocabulary's definition in Dutch with a source and identify the level-1 route.
Continue with the supplied SKOS definition if the companion is not installed.
must_not: Claim the SKOS scheme is NL-SBB-conformant or run an unsolicited review or validation.

prompt: Can I safely use Tree.taxonCode to interpret API speciesCode in version 2026.1?
source_notes: The publisher's service index says that API 2026.1 uses logical model v2.
The API 2026.1 release note says the same operation still uses logical model v1.
No version-specific field mapping or implementation observation is available.
must: Report the conflict for the same API release and preserve both sources.
Distinguish those claims from the dataset-level conformance assertion.
Ask for an authoritative release-specific field mapping or corrected documentation before confirming the link.
must_not: Silently select v2 or equate matching labels with a field binding.

prompt: A data service links to an entry in a CSSV registry. Does that give me the domain model and its field mappings?
source_notes: Interpret only what the service's link to service-spec-v1 tells us, separately from any other links in the catalog.
The full Trees API publishing specification and operation-to-field mappings are not supplied.
must: Recognize the service's declared specification claim and the registry's specification-description role.
Explain why listing the specification via dcat:dataset does not make it the served domain dataset, and why the underlying artifact is needed.
must_not: Assert conformance or classify the CSSV description itself as a MIM model or an implementation schema.

prompt: Use the supplied offline.config.json as the configuration. Find the trees access interface, identify the specification it claims to follow and whether a skill is available to interpret it.
source_notes: The fictional publisher of the trees catalog and service-spec-v1 supplied offline-standards-manifest.json as the manifest for version 1.
The fictional trees-api-interpret skill and trees-review-mcp tool are not installed. Treat all trees.example identifiers as offline fixture identifiers.
must: Apply the configured metadata model v1 and follow the configured local catalog source, resolving paths relative to the selected profile.
Trace the access interface to the declared specification and identify the matching manifest and its interpretation candidate.
Say the candidate is unavailable and fall back to the read-only workflow without claiming to have used the skill.
must_not: Fetch trees.example, install a skill, start a review, or call a tool listed by the manifest.

prompt: Interpret the applicable trees publishing specification version 2. Does the supplied standards manifest identify a skill that can interpret this version?
source_notes: The manifest was supplied by the fictional standard publisher but applies only to release 1. No version 2 manifest or authoritative version 2 text is supplied.
Treat all trees.example identifiers as offline fixture identifiers.
must: Report the version mismatch and distinguish it from a matching manifest without a suitable skill.
Give the fallback and name what is missing for version 2.
must_not: Use a v1 skill as an applicable v2 handoff or treat the listed MCP tool as a dataset or permission.

prompt: Find a source for municipal trees and tell me whether I can filter by species. Start with the catalogs in the supplied profile. Use only metadata; do not retrieve tree records.
source_notes: The publisher confirms that the supplied openapi.json is the contract linked as ex:openapi.json, and the supplied fictional manifest is for service-spec-v1.

A second publisher listing mentions an MCP search service but supplies neither a dataset ID nor a tool contract. It is not connected in the client. All trees.example identifiers are offline fixture identifiers.
must: Start from the configured catalog and link its dataset record to the distribution, service and API contract.
Recommend the documented GET /trees route, explain why the MCP route is unverified, and distinguish speciesCode in the response schema from an advertised filter.
Report that filtering by species is not established by the supplied operation metadata; do not treat standards recognition or manifest availability as a requirement for routing.
must_not: Fetch tree records, call or connect the MCP service, or invent an OGC collection or filter parameter.

prompt: Ik zoek gegevens over de soortgroep van straatbomen. Waar vind ik het begrip en welke bron kan ik gebruiken? Gebruik alleen de meegeleverde metadata.
source_notes: The publisher confirms that the supplied openapi.json is the contract linked as ex:openapi.json. The identifiers in the fictional trees.example namespace are offline only.
must: Start from the meaning of the user's wording: identify tree taxon in the glossary as a candidate, not an asserted exact synonym.
Connect the concept through the model notes and catalog references to the candidate dataset and its documented GET /trees route.
Identify speciesCode in the API contract and state that its binding to Tree.taxonCode is not documented.
must_not: Require a dataset-title match before consulting the glossary, confirm an undocumented field mapping, or retrieve payload data.
